options.how: The Classic control type keeps motion inputs such as quarter-circles for specials; Modern and Dynamic types exist as assisted alternatives.
Every special move is the special button plus a direction (neutral, side, up or down), with no motion inputs required.

sources.note: Street Fighter 6: three control types, Classic, Modern and Dynamic
Super Smash Bros. Ultimate: special moves are performed by pressing the special button, B by default

options.game: Street Fighter II: The World Warrior
options.how: Specials need joystick motions, such as down, down-forward, forward plus punch for the Hadoken, so execution itself is a skill gate.
Each fighter's specials come from the B button plus a direction, so every character shares one simple input scheme.

sources.note: Street Fighter II: Street Fighter style command inputs, Hadoken as down, down-forward, forward plus attack
Street Fighter II: 1991 landmark release of the Street Fighter series
Super Smash Bros.: special moves are the special button plus a direction

options.how: Specials and supers use motion commands, such as Kyo's quarter-circle forward plus A (236A) rekka starter, that anchor every combo.
Specials are B plus a direction, so a new player can perform every move in a character's kit from the first match.

sources.note: The King of Fighters '98: Kyo's special moves listed with motion inputs such as 236A (Ultimate Match Final Edition page)
Super Smash Bros. Melee: special moves use the special button plus a direction

options.how: Special moves need more elaborate command inputs, such as rotating the stick a quarter circle before a button press.
Neutral, Side, Up and Down Specials come from one special button plus a direction; no motion inputs anywhere in a moveset.

sources.note: Guilty Gear -Strive-: special moves require more elaborate command inputs, e.g. a quarter circle
Rivals of Aether: moves such as Neutral Special, Up Special and Down Special

options.how: Specials are motion commands like 236 and 214 on the light, medium or heavy button, as in Goku's 236H reversal.
Simple inputs perform skills with a single button press, so newcomers need not memorize complicated controls.

sources.note: Dragon Ball FighterZ: Goku's specials listed as 236M, 236H and 214L motion inputs
Granblue Fantasy Versus: Rising: simple inputs perform skills with the press of a single button

options.how: Specials and Distortion Drives use motions such as 623C and 632146D, so each character's kit is a list of commands to learn.
All moves are a single button press with no motion inputs, designed to play on keyboard or any controller.

sources.note: BlazBlue: Central Fiction: Ragna's reversals listed as 623C and 632146D
Fantasy Strike: all moves are just a single button press; simple controls

options.game: Guilty Gear XX Accent Core Plus R
options.how: Specials like Sol's Gun Flame (236P) and Volcanic Viper (623S) need quarter-circle and dragon-punch motions.
Only two buttons, Dive and Kick, and no directional inputs; fighting is reduced to spacing and timing.

sources.note: Guilty Gear XX Accent Core Plus R: Gun Flame 236P, Volcanic Viper 623S or 623H
Divekick: the first two-button fighting game, just two buttons with no d-pad

options.how: Specials and supers use motions such as 236C+D and 214214D, with an auto combo on one button as a beginner aid.
Skills can be fired with a single button press instead of a motion, so the decision, not the execution, is the test.

sources.note: Persona 4 Arena Ultimax: Yu's moves listed as 214B, 236C+D, 214214D, plus an Auto Combo
Granblue Fantasy Versus: Rising: simple inputs perform skills with a single button press

options.how: Damage is a percentage that raises knockback; a stock is lost when a fighter is launched past the stage's blast lines.
Rounds are won by emptying the opponent's health bar; at low health a player enters Rage, a glowing comeback state.

sources.note: Super Smash Bros. Ultimate: a KO occurs when a player is launched beyond the stage's blast lines
Super Smash Bros. Ultimate: damage percentage measures vulnerability to knockback
Tekken 7: Rage activates when the player's health reaches 41 points or lower, health bar glows red

options.how: Percent damage raises knockback; a KO happens when a fighter is launched past the blast lines, not when a bar empties.

options.game: Guilty Gear XX Accent Core Plus R
options.how: Rounds end when a life bar empties; each character's Guts rating cuts incoming damage further as their health falls.

sources.note: Super Smash Bros. Melee: a KO occurs when launched beyond the blast lines
Guilty Gear XX Accent Core Plus R: character stats include Damage Received Modifier and Guts

options.how: Stocks are lost by being launched off screen past the blast zones; damage percent only sets how far the next hit sends you.
Teams of three fight on health bars; in Extra mode a red low-health window unlocks free supers for a comeback.

sources.note: Super Smash Bros.: stages with blast zones; percent and knockback
Super Smash Bros.: stocks are the series' lives
The King of Fighters '98: Extra gauge red health window for free supers, growing from first to third character

options.how: Hits build damage and launch power; a strong attack sends a weakened opponent off the stage for the killing blow.
Every character has 10,000 health; tagged-out fighters recover blue health, and the team loses when all three are down.

sources.note: Rivals of Aether: platform fighter where strong attacks launch enemies for the killing blow
Dragon Ball FighterZ: every character has 10,000 health; recoverable blue health when tagged out

options.how: A stock ends when a fighter is knocked past the blast lines, so a high-percent fighter can lose it to one strong hit.
Rounds end when health empties; values vary by character, and Ragna's Drive steals life to offset his below average health.

sources.note: Super Smash Bros. Brawl: KO when launched beyond the blast lines
BlazBlue: Central Fiction: health bars, health varies by character
BlazBlue: Central Fiction: Ragna's Drive heals him to make up for below average health

options.game: Super Smash Bros. for Wii U
options.how: Stock matches are decided by launching rivals past the blast lines; the percent counter shows how far the next hit will send them.
Win by emptying the health bar; defense and guts ratings scale damage down as health passes certain thresholds.

sources.note: Super Smash Bros. for Wii U: KO when launched beyond the blast lines
Super Smash Bros. for Wii U: 2014 release
Guilty Gear -Strive-: defense and guts ratings scale damage as health passes thresholds

options.how: Stage hazards and some attacks can cause instant KOs, and otherwise a stock is lost by leaving the stage past the blast lines.
Rounds go to whoever drains the other health bar; at low health Rage adds 10% damage and unlocks Rage Arts, a late comeback threat.

sources.note: Super Smash Bros. Brawl: hazards and some attacks can cause instant KOs; normal KOs cross the blast lines
Tekken 7: at 41 health or lower Rage enables Rage Arts and Rage Drives and increases damage by 10%

options.game: Super Smash Bros. for Wii U
options.how: Optional Stamina battles aside, the default rule set KOs fighters only when they cross a blast line, so stage edges are the goal.
Each character has a fixed health value, such as Yu's 9,500, and a round ends when it is emptied.

sources.note: Super Smash Bros. for Wii U: Stamina replaces damage percentage with an HP gauge; losing all HP is a KO without crossing a blast line
Super Smash Bros. for Wii U: KO by being launched beyond the blast lines
